## Problem statement

AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ halves the enemy `bulletSpeed` of the eight shipped archetypes
across the runtime CSV, `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` and the per-entity constants.
During planning, three additional runtime fallbacks were found that also hard-code

- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — `resolveBaseConfig()`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — `groupEnemyConfig()`

Leaving them at 200 means an unknown-key enemy would fire at double the speed of
every shipped archetype, so tuning can still drift for that edge case.

consistency, updating any affected difficulty-sequencer expectations.

  documented decision is recorded to leave them at 200 with rationale).

## Problem

Several deterministic bot micro-simulations are knife-edge calibrations: a subtle, legitimate gameplay tweak (e.g. the 1-5% gentler thrust-press reduction in AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A) flips their outcomes because scores are dominated by discrete hit/bullet collisions.

During AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A two tests had to be recalibrated:
- src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts - synthetic human seed moved 7 -> 14.
- src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts - RUN_SEED moved 0x0b07 -> 0x0b16.

On the base behaviour, src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts already regressed on 13/24 seeds, and the competent-vs-legacy AC6 test only wins in base because the legacy bot chaotically collides with bullets; without bullets the legacy bot scored higher (22 vs 20) on base.

## Goal

Make these tests robust rather than seed-picked:
- Aggregate competence/style comparisons over a set of seeds (e.g. assert the styled/competent bot is not systematically worse), or
- Compare on scenarios whose score is not dominated by discrete collisions.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The style-match AC4 demonstration no longer depends on a single lucky seed (e.g. asserts over multiple seeds).
- AC2: The competent-vs-legacy AC6 test asserts an objective-based advantage rather than relying on chaotic bullet collisions.
- AC3: Recalibrating either test is not required by an unrelated small bot-feel tweak.
- AC4: Full test suite, typecheck and build pass.

# Create an improved Phase Shift effect

## Problem statement

The current Phase Shift treatment — a static dark-blue desaturation overlay plus a
cyan/red chromatic split — is not distinctive enough: when the ship phases out the
player has to look for a subtle tint to confirm it, and enemies arriving out of the
wormhole carry no visual warning at all that they are "not fully here". The ask is a
"shimmer" and "glitch" read so a phased entity is unmistakably in a different state.

## Users

- **Player (primary):** "As a player, when my ship phases out — or when enemies
  emerge from the wormhole at the start of a wave — I want them to shimmer and glitch
  so it is instantly obvious they are not in their usual state."
- **Player (defensive read):** "As a player relying on the auto Phase Shift, I want the
  effect to visibly 'fire' at the moment of activation so I can trust it and time my
  flying accordingly."
- **Developer / maintainer:** "As a developer, I want the shimmer/glitch behaviour to
  live once in the shared core/VFX layer so the shipped game and every combat gym look
  identical and cannot diverge (gym↔game parity convention)."

Example user stories:

- *"My ship phased out mid-bullet-hell and I didn't even notice — I want the screen to
  ripple and shimmer the instant phase fires, then keep pulsing so I know the state is
  still on."*
- *"Scouts poured out of the wormhole and I couldn't tell they were materialising — I
  want each one to flicker and glow as it grows, so I read 'not solid yet'."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Player phase activation burst (glitch).** On the frame the Phase Shift activates
   (`isPhased` rising edge) the screen-wide treatment emits a brief **ripple/burst**
   — e.g. a short sharp chromatic-split surge with a flicker step — that reads as a
   "glitch" hit, distinct from the player-death juice (no camera shake; the existing
   screen-wide overlays are retained).
2. **Continuous player shimmer while phased.** While `isPhased` stays true the
   treatment sustains a **continuous shimmer**: the existing cyan/red chromatic split
   becomes **more vivid and pulsing** — higher alpha (raised from 0.10 toward ~0.20),
   wider offset (raised from 3 px toward ~6 px) with a slow oscillation — plus a subtle
   alpha flicker (≈2–4 Hz) and a soft colour-pulse between the two split hues. All
   magnitudes exported as tunable constants with per-layer `PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_*`
   toggles (mirroring the current `phaseShiftJuice` pattern). Phase expiry clears every
   layer on the falling edge, leaving no residual tint.
3. **Per-enemy shimmer/glitch during wormhole emergence (no screen-space effects).**
   Each enemy growing from the wormhole gets a **per-entity** treatment over its
   growth window (`ENEMY_GROWTH_DURATION`): a brief ripple burst as it starts to
   materialise, then a continuous shimmer — a subtle scale/alpha flicker plus a soft
   colour-pulse on the entity itself — all driven from the shared spawn-animation path
   (`updateSpawnAnimation`) so `PlayScene` and every gym behave identically. No
   screen-wide overlay is introduced for the emergence path.
4. **Wormhole-position glow/pulse ring.** While a wormhole is open for a wave the
   wormhole itself gets a subtle glow/pulse ring (radius pulse + soft glow at the
   wormhole position, drawn once per wormhole, tracked in the existing
   `wormholeEffects` registry and cleared when the wormhole closes). Visually distinct
   from both the phase-shift treatment and the player-death juice.
5. **Tests and docs.** Unit tests cover: pure params model (new tunables mapped
   verbatim, toggles honoured), activation burst + continuous shimmer layer
   creation/teardown (edge-triggered, no residual layers), per-enemy shimmer driven by
   the spawn-state window, wormhole ring lifecycle, the no-camera-shake regression for
   Phase Shift, and safe-no-op behaviour headless. `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.2
   (juice) is updated with the new shimmer/glitch treatment and tunables, and code
   comments document every new constant. The full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- **No camera shake** (established producer decision — shake made Phase Shift read
  like player-death juice; the regression test asserting "never shakes" stays).
- **Gym↔game parity** (AGENTS.md): the shimmer/glitch behaviour lives once in the
  shared core/VFX layer (`src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts`, `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts`,
  the shared `CombatCoreScene`/`CombatScene` spawn path) and is consumed by both
  `PlayScene` and the gyms — no divergent copies (duplicate-body guard + gym-parity
  docs assertion apply).
- **Screen-wide effects only for the player phase path.** The enemy-emergence path is
  per-entity/per-wormhole only — the producer explicitly chose "no screen space
  effects" for spawning enemies.
- Keep the existing cyan/red split identity (producer Q3 = A: more vivid, not
  recoloured); keep per-layer toggles and the pure `resolve*Params()` pattern.
- Safe no-op without a Phaser render context (headless tests); no new runtime
  dependencies; performance-neutral (tweens/alpha only, no per-frame allocations
  beyond the existing pattern).

## Existing state

- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts` — screen-wide Phase Shift treatment: dark-blue
  dim overlay (α 0.22) + cyan/red chromatic split (α 0.1, 3 px offset), edge-triggered
  `update(active, dt)` (the `dt` param is currently unused — reserved for pulsing).
  Camera-shake regression and pure-param tests in `phaseShiftJuice.test.ts`.
- `CombatCoreScene._updatePhaseShiftJuice(dt)` lazily constructs the controller and
  drives it from `getEffectsRegistry().isPhased` — shared by `PlayScene`,
  `GymFormationScene`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`.
- `applyPhaseGhost` (`CombatEffectVisuals.ts`) sets the ship ghost alpha while phased
  (unchanged; per-entity shimmer is additive and must not fight it).
- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` — wormhole open (1 s) → enemy growth
  (`ENEMY_GROWTH_DURATION` = 1.5 s via `startSpawnAnimation`/`updateSpawnAnimation`/
  `isEnemySpawning`) → close (0.5 s); `WormholeController` guarantees at most one live
  wormhole; `spawnWormholeOpen/Close` handles.
- `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` each drive spawn updates from `updateSpawnAnimation`
  and open/close the single wormhole from `this._wormhole` with the `wormholeEffects`
  registry (`CombatScene.wormholeEffects`, cleared on `SHUTDOWN`).

## Desired change

- In `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts`: raise split alpha/offset and add a slow pulsing
  oscillation and an activation ripple/burst + continuous shimmer/flicker layer, all
  under tunables/toggles; keep edge-triggered apply/clear and the no-shake guarantee.
- In `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts`: add per-entity shimmer/glitch helpers driven from the
  spawn-growth window (burst on growth start, then flicker/pulse while growing), and a
  wormhole glow/pulse ring tied to the wormhole's open lifetime.
- Wire the per-entity shimmer into the shared spawn path so `PlayScene` and the gyms
  consume it identically; wire the wormhole ring into the existing `wormholeEffects`
  registry lifecycle.
- Update `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.2 and code comments; extend the unit tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts` — **Edit**: vivid/pulsing split, activation burst,
  continuous shimmer layers, new tunables/toggles.
- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.test.ts` — **Edit**: params, burst/shimmer, no-shake, edge
  trigger, teardown.
- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` — **Edit**: per-enemy shimmer/glitch helpers +
  wormhole glow/pulse ring.
- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.test.ts` — **Edit**: new helper tests.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `CombatScene.ts` — **Edit (minimal)**: any
  shared wiring needed to drive the new effects (e.g. pass spawn state, ring
  lifecycle) without divergent copies.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — **Edit (minimal)**: consume the shared emergence-path
  helpers; no new behaviour.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — **Edit (minimal)**: consume the same
  shared helpers (parity).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — **Edit**: §7.2 juice description + new tunables.

## Risks and assumptions

**Risks**

- *Over-stimulation / seizure sensitivity* — shimmer, flicker and glitch bursts can be
  uncomfortable. Mitigation: keep magnitudes small and durations short, drive every
  layer from exported tunables with per-layer toggles (consistent with existing juice
  practice); player shimmer uses a gentle ≈2–4 Hz flicker, not rapid strobe; a
  reduce-motion accessibility option is out of scope here (separate tracked idea).
- *Player-death overlap* — the burst must not read as death juice. Mitigation: keep
  the no-camera-shake regression, reuse the chromatic-split identity only (never the
  death ring/flash palette), and keep the burst short (~150–250 ms).
- *Parity drift* — PlayScene/gym copies diverge. Mitigation: implement once in the
  shared core/VFX modules; the repo-wide duplicate-body guard and gym-parity docs
  assertion enforce this.
- *Per-frame cost* — pulsing/flicker must not allocate per frame. Mitigation: use
  Phaser tweens and existing object reuse; no new particle emitters beyond the ring.
- *Scope creep* — the "glitch" ask could balloon into post-processing shaders.
  Mitigation: keep to the current overlay/entity technique (no render-to-texture or
  shader work); record any shader-grade effect as a separate linked item.

**Assumptions** (producer-validated via Q1–Q3)

- *Player shimmer/glitch* = activation burst then continuous shimmer, **with** the
  existing screen-wide treatment retained and made more vivid/pulsing (producer: "for
  players D — with screen space effects"; Q3 = A).
- *Emerging enemies* = per-entity shimmer/glitch (burst + shimmer) **without** any
  screen-wide effect, plus a subtle wormhole-position glow/pulse ring (producer:
  "spawning enemies D — no screen space effects"; "B + wormhole effect — no screen
  space effects").
- The existing cyan/red split palette is retained (vivid, not recoloured).
- The ship's ghost alpha (`applyPhaseGhost`) is unchanged; per-entity shimmer is
  applied to emergent enemies only, not to the player's ship object itself.
- The effect is purely cosmetic: gameplay, hitboxes and spawn protection are
  unchanged.

## Related work

See the automated "Related work (automated report)" section below (added by the
`find-related` skill).

- Phase shift needs to be auto-applied when needed (AH-0MUIYX1EE008FVS8) — *completed*;
  parent of the existing automatic Phase Shift and its juice module.
- Phase Shift juice module (AH-0MUJRGWGG0073JWS) — *completed*; the module this work
  upgrades (screen-wide dim + chromatic split, no shake).
- PlayScene: add P6 phase-shift ghost visual (AH-0MU8QVC9Y008R8I5) — *completed*; the
  ship ghost-alpha precedent (`applyPhaseGhost`).
- Victory and defeat end-of-run fanfare (audio + visual juice) (AH-0MUTV7632000ZWCB) —
  *completed*; reference for a layered, toggleable juice module and the defeat glitch
  flicker pattern.
- P6 charge and permanent auto-trigger model (AH-0MUJRGVQE004XA1T) — *completed*;
  introduced the Phase Shift auto-trigger the juice must clearly communicate.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — What specific visual effects should 'shimmer' and 'glitch' include?** Options:
  (A) rapid alpha flickering + colour cycling on the existing overlays; (B) screen-space
  distortion (pixel displacement / chromatic aberration wobble); (C) per-entity
  ripple/burst on activation + noise-like overlay flicker; (D) combination: brief
  ripple burst on activation, then continuous shimmer (flicker + subtle colour pulse).
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **D for spawning enemies (no screen space
  effects), D for players (with screen space effects).** Rationale: a brief burst on
  activation gives the 'glitch' hit, then a continuous shimmer maintains the state
  read; the agent's recommended option was D.
- **Q2 — Should enemies emerging from the wormhole receive the same screen-wide phase
  treatment or a per-enemy effect?** Options: (A) same screen-wide effect; (B) per-enemy
  personal shimmer/glow as it grows; (C) wormhole-position glow/pulse ring + standard
  screen-wide effect when phase-shift is active.
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **B + wormhole effect — no screen space
  effects.** Rationale: per-entity shimmer/glow during growth plus a subtle wormhole
  ring, with no screen-wide overlays on the emergence path.
- **Q3 — Colour palette/style for the shimmer/glitch?** Options: (A) keep the existing
  cyan/red split but more vivid (higher alpha, wider offset, pulsing); (B) purple/violet
  palette (wormhole colours); (C) neutral desaturated + subtle RGB-shift (CRT).
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A.** Rationale: preserve the established
  phase-shift identity while making it clearly more visible; the agent's recommended
  option was A.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTE8EBVD0010T0Z** – Unit tests: P6 Phase Shift - pass-through, expiry, refresh (completed)
- **AH-0MU3VQ0JR009CSIN** – Respawn player in same spot (completed)
- **AH-0MUZE4AIP009HZWC** – Make Teleport automatic like Phase Shift (free S / Down for reverse thrust) (completed)

# Intake Brief: Remove long tone from end of game sting (AH-0MV8C3HTU001X9ZP)

## Problem statement

The defeat (loss) audio sting in `GameOverScene` plays a 2.9-second sound whose sustained low-frequency drone and noise tail extend well past the five-note descending melody — making the ending feel dragged out compared to the rest of the sting.

## Users

- **Players** — experience a defeat sting that ends cleanly with the final note, matching the pacing of the main melody.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The sustained sine drone (v5, 98 Hz → 73.42 Hz) is trimmed so it ends at or before the last melody note (~1.75 s), not extending to 2.2 s.
2. The lowpass rumble tail (v6) is trimmed to match the new sting duration — no trailing rumble after the melody ends.
3. The five-note descending melody (v0–v4) is unchanged in pitch, timing, and duration.
4. The total defeat sting duration is reduced to approximately 1.8 s (±0.2 s), ending with the final note rather than trailing off.
5. All existing tests pass after the change.

## Constraints

- Only the defeat-sting recipe (`audio/toneforge/manifest.json` → `aihell-defeat-sting`) is touched.
- The baked WAV for `playDefeatStingSound` (seed 32241) must be re-rendered via the audio build pipeline.
- The Victory fanfare is unaffected.

## Existing state

- **Recipe:** `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-defeat-sting.yaml`
  - Five-note triangle melody (v0–v4): 0 – 1.75 s
  - Sine drone (v5, 98 Hz → 73.42 Hz): 0 – 2.2 s ← **the long tone**
  - LP noise tail (v6): 1.2 – 2.6 s
  - Total declared duration: 2.9 s
- **Cue:** `playDefeatStingSound` in `src/audio/effects.ts`
- **Caller:** `GameOverScene.ts` line 205 — plays the sting once on game loss

## Desired change

Shorten the sine drone's gain envelope (g5) and frequency automation (v5) so the drone ends with the last melody note (~1.75 s). Trim the noise tail (g6) to match. Update the recipe `duration` field to ~1.8 s. Re-bake the WAV.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/build-audio.sh` — re-bake the WAV via the ToneForge build pipeline
- `src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts` — no changes expected (calls existing cue)

## Related work

# Extend the headless arena to simulate the full shipped campaign (waves, levels, upgrades)

**Priority:** medium · **Issue type:** feature · **Discovered from:** <<AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW>>

## Problem statement

The automated-balancing framework (AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW) reports full balance
statistics, but two fields in its versioned schema are never populated by a
real run because the headless arena does not model campaign progression or
upgrade selection:

1. **Limit #1 — wave/level progression is not simulated.** The arena models a
   *single fixed skirmish*: a seed-derived spawn reservoir of hostiles with no
   wave sequencer, no `wave_start`/`wave_cleared`/`level_cleared` telemetry
   events, and no level transitions. Consequently `waveReached` and
   `levelReached` are **always 0** in a batch report (observed on a live
   `--batch --games 10` run), so the campaign difficulty curves
   (`src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`) cannot be tuned with this tool. Today the
   only influence the difficulty curve has is the number of hostile *reservoir*
   waves.
2. **Limit #2 — upgrade/power-up choice balance is not simulated.** The arena
   collects power-ups but never drives the upgrade-choice flow, so
   `choice_selected` events are absent and `upgradesSelected` is always
   `(none)` in the report. Per-upgrade balance therefore cannot be measured
   from bot runs.

The arena is intentionally a simplification (a "closed-loop headless arena,
not Phaser"), but the epic's own acceptance criteria claim the report captures
"wave/level reached" and "upgrades selected (per upgrade/choice id)". They are
present in the schema but empty in practice. To balance **the full campaign
shipped in the game**, the harness must exercise the same wave/level sequencer
and upgrade-choice flow that the game does — through the shared core, not a
divergent copy.

## Users

- **As a game designer / maintainer**, I want a bot batch to play the *same campaign the game ships* (all levels/waves, with upgrade choices), so I can tune per-wave difficulty targets and per-upgrade balance from evidence instead of intuition.
- **As the automated-balancing maintainer**, I want the arena to drive the shared wave sequencer and upgrade-choice system, so a change to those systems is measured by the batch.
- **As a producer**, I want the campaign-tuning evidence to come from the shipped campaign definition, so a report reflects what players experience.

## Scope

- Drive the **shared campaign/wave sequencer** (the system that consumes
  `difficulty-curves.csv` and the hand-authored `LEVELS`) inside the headless
  arena, emitting the real `wave_start` / `wave_cleared` / `level_cleared`
  telemetry the analyzer already understands, so `waveReached` and
  `levelReached` become meaningful distributions.
- Drive the **shared upgrade-choice flow** so the bot makes (or receives)
  upgrade selections and `choice_selected` events are emitted, populating
  `upgradesSelected` per choice id.
- Keep every piece of gameplay behaviour coming from the **shared core**
  (`src/scenes/core/`, `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`, the upgrade-choice
  system) — no divergent copy. This is the gym↔game parity convention: an
  enabled behaviour must run the same code in a gym/game and in the eval arena.
- Document the fidelity boundary precisely: what is now modelled (campaign
  progression, upgrade choices) and what remains simplified (VFX, formations,
  rendering).

## Non-goals

- No production runtime changes.
- No rendering/Phaser dependency in the eval core (`src/ai/eval/` stays pure:
  no wall clock, no I/O).

## Suggested approach

- Prototype sequencer integration first (spike within the item): confirm the
  shared wave sequencer and upgrade-choice system can run headless under
  Node/vitest with the same seed derivation the game uses.
- Emit the canonical telemetry records rather than inventing new event types so
  the existing metrics/balance-stats extraction picks them up unchanged.
- Extend the batch runner to optionally run a full campaign per seed (with a
  bounded tick budget), and report per-wave / per-level distributions.
- Reuse the existing determinism guarantees: same seed + config + policy ⇒
  byte-identical report, now covering the campaign path.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1: Campaign progression simulated.** A headless run plays through the shared wave/level sequencer using the shipped campaign definition (all levels and waves, including `fixed`/`curve`/`dynamic` generation modes), emitting real `wave_start`/`wave_cleared`/`level_cleared` telemetry. A batch report therefore shows non-zero, meaningful `waveReached` and `levelReached` distributions.
- **AC2: Upgrade choices simulated.** The bot makes upgrade selections through the shared upgrade-choice flow and `choice_selected` events are emitted; a batch report shows non-zero per-choice-id `upgradesSelected` distributions.
- **AC3: Single source of truth.** The arena consumes the shared wave sequencer / upgrade-choice system directly (asserted by test and the existing duplicate-body/parity guards); no divergent copy of campaign, enemy, ship or upgrade stats exists in `src/ai/eval/`.
- **AC4: Determinism preserved.** Same seed + config + policy ⇒ byte-identical campaign report; `recordsHash` stable; no wall-clock/IO in the pure eval core.
- **AC5: Config sensitivity.** Editing `difficulty-curves.csv` (e.g. raising a wave's `targetDifficulty`) and/or an upgrade definition measurably changes the corresponding report distribution for the same seeds, verified by test.
- **AC6: Fidelity boundary documented.** `docs/BALANCING.md` (and/or `docs/EVALUATION.md`) states exactly what campaign behaviour is now modelled and what remains simplified, so consumers do not over-read the report.
- **AC7: Tests.** Campaign progression, upgrade-choice emission, single-source-of-truth, config sensitivity and determinism are covered by unit tests; no wall-clock/IO leaks into the pure core.
- **AC8: Bounded resources.** A full-campaign batch over ~100 games still completes in a practical time and bounded memory on a dev machine (incremental aggregation, per-run summaries only).
- **AC9: All related documentation is updated** (code comments, `docs/BALANCING.md`, `docs/EVALUATION.md`, README).
- **AC10: Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Risks, assumptions and mitigations

- **Fidelity risk:** running the real sequencer headless may pull in Phaser-coupled code. *Mitigation:* confirm the shared core's headless-safety during the spike; keep the pure eval layer free of rendering.
- **Scope-creep risk:** this item is about *simulating* the campaign, not retuning it. Actual tuning changes remain separate work items.
- **Parity risk:** a divergent arena copy would violate gym↔game parity (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1). *Mitigation:* consume the shared core; rely on the existing equivalence guards.
- **Determinism risk:** campaign RNG (dynamic/curve generation) must derive from the run seed exactly as the game does. *Mitigation:* reuse `createSeededRng` and the game's seed derivation; test byte-identical replay.

## Related work

- **Automated Balancing** (AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW) — the framework this extends.
- **Automate the balance-tuning loop** (AH-0MV8Q5EYE001R715) — the comparison loop that will consume these richer reports.
- **Collect balance statistics from human player games (dev mode only)** (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) — shares the schema; becomes directly comparable once campaign stats are populated.
- **Periodically validate the human experience against the intended experience** (AH-0MV7WVHU0000U775) — depends on richer campaign evidence.
- **Integrate enemy classification into wave generation and balance tooling** (AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP) — balance-rule consumer.
- Docs: `docs/BALANCING.md`, `docs/EVALUATION.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`.

# Audio Design Chapter — retro-arcade survival game GDD

## Problem statement

The GDD currently defines only SFX (§7.3 Audio Direction) and states background music is out of MVP scope with no musical direction defined. The game lacks a documented musical identity (scales, motifs, harmonic language, instrumentation, dynamic mixing, and state-driven music architecture) to guide composition and implementation when music is eventually built.

## Users

- **Audio designers and composers** — need a definitive musical language (scales/modes, motifs, progressions, instrumentation palette) to write consistent, on-brief music.
- **Technical audio programmers** — need the implementation contract (bus architecture, priority tiers, ducking, state machine, middleware guidance) to build or integrate the music system.
- **Game designers / producers** — need per-game-state emotional targets and transition rules to keep audio aligned with gameplay pacing.

User stories:

- As an audio designer, I want documented scales and motifs per game state, so my compositions match the game's emotional arc without guesswork.
- As a technical audio programmer, I want the music state machine and dynamic-mixing rules defined, so I can implement or configure the music engine against a fixed contract.
- As a producer, I want music explicitly scoped as design reference (out of MVP), so the shipped SFX scope (§7.3) is not disturbed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — New chapter file created:** The full brief supplied by the producer (10 sections: Introduction & Audio Vision; Musical Identity; Recommended Scales & Modes; Melodic Motifs; Chord Progressions by Game State; Instrumentation Palette; Dynamic Mixing Rules; State-Driven Music Transitions; Implementation Guidelines; Playtesting & Iteration) is saved as a Markdown GDD addendum document (predicted path `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md`), with the content preserved verbatim from the approved brief.
- [ ] **AC2 — GDD §7.3 references the chapter:** The "Background Music" subsection in GDD §7.3 (Audio Direction) is updated to link the new chapter file, while retaining the explicit statement that background music is **out of MVP scope** (design reference only; SFX remains the only in-scope audio).
- [ ] **AC3 — GDD §8 future-scope row updated:** The "Background music" row in §8 (Future Scope) references the new chapter file so the doc stays self-consistent.
- [ ] **AC4 — Doc-only change, no behaviour impact:** No game code, SFX behaviour, or runtime audio pipeline is changed; existing §7.3 SFX scope and the shipped ToneForge pipeline remain authoritative for the MVP.
- [ ] **AC5 — Validation:** The new chapter's cross-references are verified (file exists, links resolve, internal section headings matched to the brief); all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including any index/table-of-contents entries in the GDD.
- [ ] **AC6 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** (docs-only; confirms no accidental code impact).

## Constraints

- Music remains **"design reference, out of MVP scope"** — no change to the existing scope stance in GDD §7.3 or §8.
- The chapter content is **producer-approved** — reproduce it verbatim (author: Ross; version 1.0; dated 16 October 2026).
- Follow the repo's docs naming/style conventions where sensible (singular Markdown addendum under `docs/`, referenced by relative link).
- UK English throughout.

## Existing state

- GDD §7.3 "Audio Direction" covers MVP SFX: baked ToneForge WAV pipeline, SFX event catalogue, per-enemy/per-player audio character, beat-synced explosion accents, and a one-paragraph "Background Music" subsection stating music is a nice-to-have, out of MVP.
- GDD §8 "Future Scope" lists "Background music — Synthwave / retro electronic soundtrack" with no further detail.

## Desired change

- Add the full Audio Design Chapter as a standalone GDD addendum document.
- Point GDD §7.3's "Background Music" subsection and §8's future-scope row at the new document.
- Keep all gameplay/SFX/runtime behaviour untouched.

**Key Files:**
- `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` (new) — the full Audio Design Chapter addendum (predicted filename; confirm at implementation)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 "Background Music" subsection updated with a link + scope note; §8 "Background music" row updated with a link

## Related work

- **Update audio documentation (AH-0MUTYV9QV0000HDT)** — completed; ToneForge baked-asset pipeline docs; source of the current §7.3 scope language.

- **Scope-stance divergence (medium):** the chapter is "APPROVED FOR PRODUCTION" in tone while the GDD keeps music out of MVP. Mitigated by AC2/AC3 explicitly framing the chapter as design reference; implementation remains a future work item.
- **Middleware references (FMOD/Wwise) are forward-looking:** the game currently uses Phaser/Web Audio with baked assets (§7.3). The chapter's §9 middleware guidance is design intent for future integration, not an instruction to adopt FMOD/Wwise in the MVP. Noted in the chapter context if needed.

# Dev-mode write-back: gym "Save to repo" persists bot tuning to src/data/bot-tuning.json

**Priority:** medium · **Issue type:** feature

**discovered-from:** AH-0MV9GZD2C005IIU3

## Summary

Today the Bot Tuning gym persists only to `localStorage` (`ai-hell-bot-tuning`), and the Git-tracked shipped baseline `src/data/bot-tuning.json` must be refreshed manually via the gym **Export** button → overwrite file → commit (documented in `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §12 and `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`). Player ship and enemy/difficulty configs already have a dev-mode write-back path: the Vite CSV plugin (`vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`, served `/api/csv/...` PUT endpoints) writes gym Save/Save-As edits straight into the committed CSVs (`src/core/configStore.ts` `saveShipConfig`/`saveEnemyConfig`). This item gives bot tuning the same convenience: a dev-mode (Vite-serve-only) write path that persists the currently-selected tuning configuration to `src/data/bot-tuning.json`, so a designer does not have to Export → overwrite → commit manually.

## User stories

- As a designer tuning the demo bot, I want a Save action in the Bot Tuning gym to write my current tuning back to `src/data/bot-tuning.json` (dev server only), so the shipped baseline stays in sync without the manual Export → overwrite → commit dance.
- As a maintainer, I want the write path to be dev-only and explicit, so a production/static build can never mutate the committed baseline or surprise a distributed user.

## Desired change

1. **Write endpoint** — expose a dev-only endpoint (e.g. `PUT /api/bot-tuning/`) in the Vite config plugin chain, or reuse/parallel the `configCsvPlugin` pattern, that writes the exact `serialiseBotTuningState()` JSON blob to `src/data/bot-tuning.json` atomically (temp file + rename, matching the CSV plugin) and validates the shape before writing (reuse `parseState`-style validation / `coerceTuningValues`).
2. **Gym affordance** — add a "Save to repo" (dev-only) button in the Bot Tuning gym panel, next to Export, that posts the current store state to the endpoint and reports success/failure (`SaveResult`-shaped, like `saveShipConfig`). Disabled or hidden outside dev (`import.meta.env.DEV`, matching `saveShipConfig`'s `isDev()` gate).
3. **Out-of-scope guard** — no runtime behaviour change and no new write path in production; same guard contract as the CSV store (`WRITE_UNAVAILABLE` outside dev). Atomic replace must preserve the trailing-newline/pretty-print format the `bot-tuning.json` tests expect (`src/data/bot-tuning.test.ts` asserts byte-identity with the store Export plus trailing newline).
4. **Tests** — unit tests for the write helper (valid blob replaces file; invalid blob rejected without touching the file; non-dev returns unavailable; byte round-trip with `serialiseBotTuningState()`), gym-level test that "Save to repo" calls the write path and reflects a real file write, and a plugin-endpoint test mirroring `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` scope. `npm run typecheck` and the full suite stay green; the gym↔game duplicate-body parity guard stays green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Dev-only write endpoint persists the baseline.** In dev mode, a write of the current `serialiseBotTuningState()` blob updates `src/data/bot-tuning.json` atomically; the file stays byte-identical to the store Export (pretty-print + trailing newline), so `src/data/bot-tuning.test.ts` round-trip tests pass after the write.
- **AC2 — Invalid input never corrupts the file.** A write with an invalid/unschematised blob fails with a clear `SaveResult` reason and leaves the committed file untouched.
- **AC3 — Production/static builds cannot write.** The endpoint is dev-serve-only and the client gate (`isDev()`) means a production build reports `WRITE_UNAVAILABLE` (no mutation of the shipped baseline).
- **AC4 — Gym affordance.** The Bot Tuning gym exposes a dev-only "Save to repo" control that persists the current selection and reports success/failure; hidden/disabled outside dev.
- **AC5 — Tests + validation.** Unit + gym + plugin-endpoint tests cover persistence, rejection, round-trip, and non-dev unavailability; `npm run typecheck`, the full suite, and the parity guard pass.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — the CSV dev-write pattern to parallel/clone for bot tuning
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `saveShipConfig`/`saveEnemyConfig` + `SaveResult`/`WRITE_UNAVAILABLE` contract to mirror
- `src/core/botTuningStore.ts` — `serialiseBotTuningState()`, `parseState`/`coerceTuningValues` validation, `BOT_TUNING_SCHEMA_VERSION`
- `src/data/bot-tuning.json` — the committed baseline the dev write targets
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts` — new "Save to repo" control next to Export
- `src/data/bot-tuning.test.ts` — file round-trip/trailing-newline contract the writer must preserve
- Docs: `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §12, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — update the refresh workflow (dev write vs Export)

## Constraints

- No change to bot decision/permission semantics — only a dev-tool persistence path (same scope boundary recorded in AH-0MV9GZD2C005IIU3).
- Follows the CSV plugin precedent exactly (atomic write, allowed-path allowlist, `apply: serve` only); do not invent a new infra pattern.
- The stored file must stay Git-committable and byte-stable (test contract).
- Out of scope: automatic background sync on every slider move (that would spam writes); the affordance must be an explicit Save action.

# MysteryUfoDrone collector entity

## Summary

Implement the visible collector drone as a shared-core entity: a code-drawn
scaled copy of the player ship that seeks minerals, vacuums them within its
collector radius, returns home and pays out.

## Target outcome

`src/entities/MysteryUfoDrone.ts` is a self-contained neon-vector entity with
the full seek → collect → return → payout lifecycle, lifetime/capacity
termination, and the agreed destruction contract.

## Minimal implementation

- New `MysteryUfoDrone` entity following the `Harvester` seek pattern
  (`setSeekTargets` + nearest-live-mineral steering) and the code-drawn
  graphics convention (no external art).
- Constructor takes the resolved level values (lifetime, capacity, radius).
- State machine: SEEK → COLLECT (vacuum minerals whose centre enters the
  radius) → RETURN (when full or lifetime expires) → PAYOUT → gone.
- Expose read-only accessors for tests (state, held minerals, target).
- Destruction contract: `onEnemyBullet`/`onEnemyBody` mark it destroyed and
  expose held minerals for the drop; a player-bullet check is a no-op.
- Unit tests (`MysteryUfoDrone.test.ts`) for the lifecycle and destruction.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Level-0 drone: lifetime 5 s, capacity 10 minerals, collector radius 20 px,
  all overridable from resolved level data.
- The drone actively seeks the nearest live mineral, collects minerals whose
  centre enters its collector radius, returns to the player and pays out
  when it has collected its capacity **or** its lifetime expires (whichever
  comes first), and disappears after payout — verified by unit tests
  asserting the seek → collect → return → pay out flow.
- Termination fires on either capacity reached **or** lifetime expiry,
  whichever comes first, and the drone disappears after payout with exactly
  the held minerals in the pay-in.
- An enemy bullet or enemy body collision destroys the drone and exposes its
  held minerals for the drop; the player's own fire cannot destroy it.
- The drone is rendered as a scaled-down player-ship entity, code-drawn
  neon-vector, no external art.

## Parent AC covered

Covers parent AC2 (seek/collect/return/payout flow, lifetime/capacity
termination, level-0 defaults) and the destruction behaviour of AC5.

# Shared-core drone lifecycle pass

## Summary

Add the shared spawn/tick/teardown pass over the drone in the shared core so
the game and every gym run one identical implementation (gym↔game parity).

## Target outcome

A `src/scenes/core/` helper (mirroring `dropLayer.ts` / `mineralLayer.ts`)
that spawns drones, feeds them the live mineral field each tick, drains their
earned minerals into the scene's hold and converts a destroyed drone into
field deposits.

## Minimal implementation

- New shared helper (e.g. `combatDrone.ts`) with `spawnDrone`, `tickDrones`,
  `drainPayouts` and `teardownDrones`-style functions, pure where possible.
- Feed the live mineral field to each drone through `setSeekTargets`
  (reuse `enemyTargeting.pushSeekTargets` style) each shared tick.
- Route the drone's pay-in minerals into the caller-supplied hold sink; on
  destruction, drop held minerals plus a `2 × level` bonus as collectable
  field deposits via the existing mineral/drop layer.
- Wire the pass into `CombatCoreScene`/`CombatScene` ordering so both
  `PlayScene` and gyms inherit it.
- Tests for spawn/tick/payout/destruction-drop at the helper level.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The helper is the only place drone spawn/tick/teardown/payout logic lives;
  no per-scene copy exists (verified by the duplicate-body guard).
- Feeding the live mineral field makes the drone actively seek the nearest
  live mineral and collect minerals whose centre enters its collector
  radius; an empty field clears its target and it holds station.
- Payout minerals reach the supplied hold sink exactly once per drone when
  it returns to the player.
